Identity.History: Classical Thebes was inland, on the Boeotian plain, so it had no urban waterfront or port of its own. Thebes nevertheless had access to several Boeotian harbors. Anthedon, on the Euboean Gulf, is the strongest candidate for a port closely associated with Theban naval activity; Strabo explicitly describes it as a harbor city, and modern scholarship commonly connects it with Thebes’ fleet-building efforts in the 360s BC. On the Corinthian Gulf, Kreusis was another important nearby harbor, though it is more specifically identified as the port of Thespiae, not Thebes. Boeotia also had access to places such as Siphai, Thisbe, and Larymna.
